summary: PR #9 is mostly a mechanical directory consolidation, but it sneaks a broader governance declaration into the ADR and leaves a wording contradiction about every registry child being a semantic class while putting many cross-cutting flat files directly at the root.

findings.issue: A registry path-consolidation ADR declares `grit/rtk/icm/vox` deprecated and no longer required going forward. That is a scope jump: tool-governance retirement is not the same decision as moving `registries/cross-cutting` to `registry`, and it conflicts with agent guidance that still names sanctioned primitives until formally replaced.
findings.remediation: Remove this paragraph from ADR-0115 and land tool-governance retirement in its own ADR/spec update with the actual operating-contract changes.

findings.issue: The ADR says every direct child of `registry/` is a semantic class, then immediately permits flat cross-cutting files such as `registry/microservices.json`, `registry/fixuptasks.jsonl`, and `registry/mistakes-ledger.json` at the same level as class directories. The naming rule is not actually the rule the migration applies.
findings.remediation: Either say `registry/` may contain class directories plus legacy/root-level singleton registries, or put the singleton files under an explicit semantic class directory. Do not describe a stricter invariant than the tree enforces.

findings.issue: The migration relies on broad reference rewrites but does not add a machine check that forbids live `registries/cross-cutting` path reintroduction. Without a small gate, this cleanup will regress into another grep sweep.
findings.remediation: Add or extend a retired-vocabulary/path-token lane scoped to live code/config/specs/docs (excluding historical evidence) so the old path cannot come back.
